sections.title: High-Level Concept of Embedded Figures
sections.content: Level 3 questions involve highly complex line networks, 3D-to-2D projections, multi-layered intersections, and rotated shape fitting. You must mentally construct the entire geometry from the description and carefully analyze hidden complex polygons such as kites, rhombuses, and irregular parallelograms.

sections.title: 3D to 2D Projection Understanding
sections.content: Example: The 2D front view of a transparent cube where all four body diagonals are visible. Step 1: Visualize the front square face of the cube. Step 2: Imagine the back face visible through transparency. Step 3: Draw all body diagonals connecting opposite vertices. Step 4: Observe the intersecting diagonal mesh formed in 2D. Step 5: Identify closed shapes such as rhombuses or parallelograms formed by diagonal intersections.

sections.title: Multi-Level Line Structures
sections.content: Example: A large regular octagon where all lines connecting opposite vertices are drawn. Step 1: Visualize the 8-sided polygon. Step 2: Connect each pair of opposite vertices. Step 3: Observe the central intersection region. Step 4: Identify smaller triangles formed by intersections. Step 5: Look for complex polygons such as kites (two pairs of adjacent equal sides) and rhombuses (all sides equal).

sections.title: Rotated Shape Embedding
sections.content: Question Type: If Option B is rotated by 135 degrees, will it embed into the large figure? Step 1: Identify angles and side lengths of Option B. Step 2: Mentally rotate the shape by 135 degrees (90 + 45). Step 3: Track how each vertex shifts position. Step 4: Compare the rotated edges with the lines in the large figure. Step 5: Confirm whether all sides align perfectly.

sections.title: 4–6 Step Solved Example 1
sections.content: Question: How many rhombuses are embedded in the 2D projection of a transparent cube with body diagonals? Solution: Step 1: Identify all diagonal intersections. Step 2: Detect sets of four equal-length sides forming closed shapes. Step 3: Separate small and medium rhombuses. Step 4: Check symmetry to avoid double counting. Step 5: Add totals carefully.

sections.title: 4–6 Step Solved Example 2
sections.content: Question: How many kites are present in an octagon with opposite vertices connected? Solution: Step 1: Focus on the central intersection area. Step 2: Combine adjacent triangles to form kite shapes. Step 3: Verify two pairs of adjacent equal sides. Step 4: Count small kites first. Step 5: Identify larger composite kites. Step 6: Sum all valid kites.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Misinterpreting 3D structures in 2D. 2. Ignoring symmetry and double counting shapes. 3. Incorrectly rotating shapes mentally. 4. Failing to verify side equality in complex polygons.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 3 requires advanced spatial visualization, structured multi-step counting, and careful geometric verification. Always construct the figure layer by layer, check symmetry, verify side lengths and angles, and confirm rotated alignments before concluding.

tricks.title: Layer-by-Layer Visualization
tricks.explanation: Break complex 3D projections into front, back, and diagonal layers.
tricks.example: Visualize the cube’s front square before adding diagonals.

tricks.title: Symmetry Advantage
tricks.explanation: Use symmetry to multiply counts instead of recounting similar regions.
tricks.example: If one rhombus exists on one side of an octagon, similar ones may exist symmetrically.

tricks.title: Intersection Mapping
tricks.explanation: Mark mentally where multiple lines intersect; these areas form most complex polygons.
tricks.example: The center of an octagon often contains maximum kites.

tricks.title: Rotation Anchor Method
tricks.explanation: Choose one vertex as an anchor and rotate the rest around it mentally.
tricks.example: Fix one corner and imagine other points shifting 135 degrees.

tricks.title: Equal Side Confirmation
tricks.explanation: For rhombus or kite detection, verify equal side lengths carefully.
tricks.example: All four sides must match for a rhombus.

tricks.title: Complex to Simple Breakdown
tricks.explanation: Reduce complicated meshes into smaller triangles and quadrilaterals first.
tricks.example: Count all small triangles before forming larger kites.

tricks.title: Avoid Double Counting
tricks.explanation: Track counted shapes systematically to prevent repetition.

tricks.title: Multi-Step Verification
tricks.explanation: After completing 4–6 steps, re-evaluate the figure from a different orientation.
tricks.example: Rotate the entire mental image 90 degrees and check alignment again.
